depth_findings.text: validateEndpoint accepts any https URL and the sender then POSTs a VAPID-signed request to it, so any organisation member can make notification-core send requests to arbitrary https hosts (blind request forgery). Restrict accepted endpoints to the push-service hosts classifyEndpoint names, or refuse non-public addresses at dial time, before NOTIFICATION_WEB_PUSH_ENABLED is turned on anywhere.

Native notices delivered through the queued DeliveryWorker (NOTIFICATION_DELIVERY_WORKER_ENABLED=true) never reach notifyPush, so no Web Push goes out on that path. Add the same hook after MarkDeliverySubmitted before enabling push together with the worker.

Subscriptions are not erased when an organisation is purged: org_deletion_consumer.go subscribes to pending, reminder and cancelled only, and org-core publishes no purge subject, so sealed endpoints outlive the org. This needs an org-core purge event, a CONTROLPLANE consumer binding and an ACL line in control-shared-nats.conf (Control Plane owned).

The definition of done is unproved: rebuild notification-core and the production SPA, set NOTIFICATION_WEB_PUSH_ENABLED=true, subscribe a Chrome profile, run a gated approval with the tab closed, and capture the OS notification, the outbound push at a stub push service (body is the constant wake-up), empty Cache storage, and that a revoked endpoint stops receiving.

Chrome requires a visible notification for each push (userVisibleOnly). The worker returns without one when a window is visible, so Chrome may show its own generic notice. Verify live and decide whether to show then close a silent notice.

Installability is unverified: the worker has no fetch handler by design, so the install prompt on the production build must be checked against current Chrome and Edge rules. Safari and iOS are untested and must stay recorded as untested.
The owner must decide whether an email channel ships with WS16-S6. Native types have no email delivery (D2-798), so the section offers in-app and push only.

A browser keeps its subscription after sign-out or an account change, and the same endpoint can be registered under two users of one organisation, so both keep receiving wake-ups on a shared device. Revoke other rows with the same endpoint hash on subscribe and unsubscribe on sign-out.

enablePushOnThisDevice reuses an existing PushSubscription without comparing its applicationServerKey, so after a VAPID rotation the device stays subscribed to a dead key. Rotation invalidates every subscription and needs a documented procedure.

notifyPush starts one goroutine per submitted notice, each making up to ten sends with ten-second timeouts, and registrations have no per-user cap. Add a bounded worker and a registration cap before a burst or abuse.

store_pg_test.go (TestWebPushSubscriptionsAgainstRealPostgres) is written but not run; it needs NOTIFICATION_CORE_TEST_DATABASE_URL and NOTIFICATION_CORE_ALLOW_DB_MUTATION=1 against a disposable Postgres with migration 016 applied.

depth_findings.text: With EXECUTION_CORE_THREAD_WORKSPACE=true before WS22-S3 mints the sandbox bearer for thread turns, every non-ZDR governed run that names a thread is refused at RunAgent (run_agent demands the bearer); keep the switch off until S3, or add an optional bearer read in auth.rs (not owned) so Do runs degrade to ephemeral.

A file the program creates or overwrites above 8 MiB is never offered to the thread, and a save of such a call still reads state 'synced' with the old version kept; S3 must report skipped paths in the workspace result.

When the program run itself fails (execution error), attach_workspace leaves the result without a workspace object, so the model is not told whether the call's files were saved or refused; S3 must add the workspace report on the error path.
execute_thread_code_interpreter is not exercised end to end (the code run needs the Linux bwrap sandbox); a Linux container run with the switch on is required before S3.
The in-process fake sandbox-manager encodes the thread RPC contract as read from the S1 design, not the Go server; conflict and revision semantics still need a Go-side or live check.
ensure_thread_lease's happy path (a real AcquireLease with scope_type thread through the client) is not unit-tested; only the ZDR refusal and the cache are.

The thread lease cache can serve a lease released out of band for up to 30 minutes, so thread calls fail until the entry ages out; on a not-found from GetThreadWorkspace, evict the cache entry and re-acquire once.

The plan's zdr-posture-matrix row is not added (no feature-refusal shape in the matrix schema; no existing feature refusal has a row); the owner should confirm the NAMED_SITES entry is the enforcement of record for feature refusals.
A delegated child run (depth > 0) takes the thread path and shares its parent's thread workspace; decide whether children inherit thread files the way attachments are withheld (WS08-S6).
Two runs in the same thread serialise their whole program runs behind the per-thread lock, held through the code execution timeout; acceptable for v1, but a long program blocks the other run.
Every thread-scope call downloads all of the thread's files again (up to 256 files and 64 MiB); the plan's optional hash-keyed blob cache is not built.

ThreadWorkspace::hydrate and commit repeat the loops of workspace_hydrate::hydrate and diff_and_upload because the thread path needs scoped CAS keys; a shared loop taking a fetch or put closure would remove the duplicate when S4 changes the Space path.

attach_workspace parses and re-serialises the CodeResult JSON, so with the switch on the key order of the tool output changes (BTreeMap ordering); harmless to the model, but it is a visible difference.

The DoD proof (turn 2 reads turn 1's file through two run ids; exec-core restart between turns loses nothing; redaction reported) needs the WS22-S3 flow with the three flags on and a rebuilt stack; not run here, per the brief.

With EXECUTION_CORE_THREAD_WORKSPACE=true, run_agent demands the user-bound sandbox bearer for every non-ZDR run that names a thread (grpc.rs, `space_id.is_empty() && !thread_workspace`). Until WS22-S3 mints that bearer, every such governed run is refused at RunAgent, so the switch must stay off until S3.

A baseline file the program grows past 8 MiB is skipped. So is one it replaces with a symlink or a directory (is_syncable or collect_relative_paths skip it, and diff_deletions sees it still exists). It is neither updated nor deleted, yet the report says state 'synced'. The commit must report skipped paths before the switch flips.
When the program run fails, attach_workspace returns the error unchanged, so the model never learns whether the call's files were saved, refused or conflicted (commit still ran).

With the switch on and no CAS client (MinIO unset), workspace_sync::open fails with Unavailable and execute_thread_code_interpreter fails the whole code_interpreter call. It does not degrade to the per-call ephemeral path.

The thread lease cache (30 min) can serve a lease that was released or expired out of band. Until the entry ages out, every thread call fails with HydrateFailed. On a NotFound or FailedPrecondition from GetThreadWorkspace, evict the entry and re-acquire once.

With the switch off: thread_for_step returns None, so the sandbox-bearer gate, the Space context, and the code_interpreter arm take the same branches as before; the workspace_cas put/get refactor keeps the same keys. New module workspace_sync.rs: open() hydrates a thread's files from GetThreadWorkspace into a fresh per-call directory (Drop removes it); commit() uploads changed files under thread/<org>/<thread>/ (scrubbed; redacted paths reported), sends deletions, reports conflicts without overwriting, refuses over 256 files / 64 MiB before any upload, and never keeps program, .tmp, .mplconfig, __pycache__, attachments/ or files over 8 MiB. Runtime: a thread-scope code_interpreter call (ExecuteStep or Do run, non-Space, non-persistence-free, switch on) takes ensure_thread_lease (scope_type thread, cached per run and thread, 30 min < lease TTL), holds a per-thread lock from hydrate to save, runs the program in the hydrated directory and attaches a 'workspace' object to the result. ExecuteStepRequest.thread_id = 13 feeds the workspace only; memory tools still get an empty thread id on the direct RPC. Zero-retention and waived steps never take the thread path; ensure_thread_lease and open() refuse persistence-free calls with the typed sandbox_workspace refusal. depth_findings.text: Rollout default: the row says CRON_CONTRACT_GUARDS_ENABLED defaults true once S4 is on, but the batch rule says every new switch defaults off. The code defaults off (only the literal true enables). The owner or lead must set the rollout default before the switch goes on.

In-place renewal is not built. The PATCH refuses a bare re-enable of a lapsed approval, but the row's 'PATCH un-pausing requires renewal (new template + new Control create decision)' would need the gateway PATCH route to obtain a Control create decision and capability-core PATCH to bind it; those files are not owned. Today renewal creates a new schedule through ScheduleDialog and the expired paused schedule stays until deleted. The owner should accept new-schedule renewal or schedule the in-place path.
Renewal cannot grant any tool yet: DELEGABLE_SCHEDULE_TOOLS is empty in schedule-from-chat.ts, so the renewal dialog creates a draft-only schedule until the registry-backed tool list lands.

Live proof not run (lead, Docker rules): rebuild capability-core and the frontend; with the flag on in dev and a schedule whose approval expires in about two minutes, confirm one paused_expired fire row, one notice to the creator, a 409 on bare PATCH enable, and the renewal path in a panel screenshot. Requires SCHEDULE_CONTRACT_ENABLED on and a Control-signed contract, since the UI cannot create one yet.

The legacy pending-fire sweep runs for every schedule when the switch is on, not only contract schedules as the flag text says. Pre-S1 fires never belong to contract schedules, and the 0056 migration comment says S8 sweeps all of them, so a contract-only filter would make the sweep a no-op. The owner should confirm; restricting it is a one-line join on task_template.

Expiry is enforced at the next due slot, not at the expiry instant. A daily schedule can stay enabled up to a day after its approval expires, so the pause and its notice are late. No fire happens in that window because the S5 dispatcher refuses an expired contract at dispatch.
Pause notices are sent after the batch commits with no retry and no outbox. A crash between commit and send loses the notice, though the paused fire row still records the pause.

Pauses cannot use the S7 envelope path: runwatch.processScheduledOutcome requires a run id and thread id, which a pause does not have. S8 sends the same notification type directly through notifyclient. runwatch could accept pause outcomes later (file not owned).

The failure count reads cron_fires.status = 'failed', not cron_fires.outcome as the row says, because the sweeper's own failed fires have an empty outcome. For scheduled-step failures S1 writes both, so the two agree there.

With the switch on, the legacy sweep runs UPDATE cron_fires WHERE status='pending' AND fire_key='' every minute, and no index covers status. A partial index on cron_fires (status) WHERE status='pending' AND fire_key='' would be needed at scale; it is a later migration, not this slice.

No DB-backed test yet for the paused INSERT against the real cron_fires columns from 0056 (an integration test would extend sweeper_failure_integration_test.go), and no test that RunOnce gates the legacy sweep on the switch (RunOnce needs a pool). Unit tests cover sweepDue, the streak, the contract reader, the PATCH and the panel.

The panel's renewal and expiry label are not behind a switch. They show only for schedules that carry an approval, which exist only when SCHEDULE_CONTRACT_ENABLED is on. With S8 off, a lapsed approval still cannot be resumed from the panel, although the server would accept a bare enable.

'paused' is a new cron_fires status token. The status comment in session-core migration 0004 (pending | running | completed | failed) and the 'unknown' word from 0056 are now out of date. Those docs are not owned, so they were not updated.

results.notes: WS20-S8 built in wave mode with every new switch off by default. Backend (capability-core): Sweeper.WithContractGuards turns the guards on, and only then does the sweeper read a schedule's approval_contract (JSONB text under task_template, per S4). An expired or unreadable approval pauses the schedule before any Control authorization: enabled=false plus a cron_fires row with status 'paused' and outcome 'paused_expired'. Three most recent fires all 'failed' pause it as 'paused_failures' before a fourth fire. Pending fires with an empty fire_key older than one hour become 'unknown' (the S1 migration 0056 comment names this sweep). Each pause queues a notice of type modelplane.scheduled_run_outcome to the creator (content-free: fixed copy, closed outcome, schedule id), sent after the batch commits through Sweeper.WithPauseNotifier. CronHandler.WithContractGuards makes PATCH refuse enabled=true on a lapsed approval with 409 and no write. Frontend: each row shows the approval expiry; a lapsed approval replaces Resume with 'Forny godkjenning', which opens the existing ScheduleDialog seeded with the schedule's name and goal; paused fires get a 'Pauset' label. No migration, no proto, no session-core or gateway change. Off path verified: with the guards off the sweeper reaches the fire authorizer exactly as before and the PATCH writes as before. Prerequisites confirmed present: S4 (0a3a21909), S5, S7 (19eee698b, notification-core migration 017 already allowlists the type), and S1's migration 0056 for fire_key and outcome. The worktree is shared with other slices of this batch (for example apps/Model Plane/docs/sse-event-taxonomy.md shows a modification I did not make); I touched none of their files. Live proof and rebuilds were not run (lead).
